model: REIT distributable income (AFFO) capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.sbc_source: Management fees paid in units, FY25/26 annual report statement of distribution (S$6.646m); added back in distributable income but a real cost settled in new units, so charged in the flow via sbc_pct_path (~1.0% of gross revenue).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T09:04:18Z (SGX regular session, Yahoo Finance chart API)
inputs.share_count_basis: Units in issue at 31 Mar 2026 (FY25/26 annual report). Held flat: the only recurring issuance is management fees paid in units, which is charged in the flow instead (charging both would double-count). Equity-funded acquisitions are assumed value-neutral and are excluded from the growth paths.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in SGD, not WACC: distributable income is already after interest and after perpetual-securities distributions. SGS 10y ~2.3-2.5% + beta ~0.9 x ERP ~5.5% => ~7.3-7.5%. Base 7.5%, bull 7.0%, bear 8.0% (bear also prices the NA data-centre concentration and swap repricing).
inputs.lease_treatment: Land-lease (JTC) payments are inside property expenses / NPI and therefore already inside distributable income; no separate lease charge (lease_cost_pct_path 0).
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is immaterial (S$2.5m equity); distributable income is the amount attributable to Unitholders.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT -> routed per dcf-methods SKILL.md to AFFO/distributable-income capitalisation at the cost of equity, run through the component engine with net_debt held at ZERO (subtracting the S$2.35bn of borrowings and the S$600m of perpetual securities would deduct financing twice: both are already paid out of distributable income). Engine mapping: revenue = gross revenue (S$673.0m FY26); 'EBITDA margin' = distributable income to Unitholders / gross revenue (FY26 54.1%, Q4 FY26 run-rate 54.0%); 'SBC' = management fees paid in units; 'capex' = maintenance/re-leasing capex not funded by distributable income (2.5% base; data-centre re-letting of NA enterprise space needs TI/fit-out); D&A and cash tax 0 (DI is post-tax; tax-transparent S-REIT). FY0 owner flow = 363.9 - 6.6 - 16.8 = S$340.4m = 11.9c/unit vs reported DPU 12.71c. FY26 revenue includes ~4.5 months of the Singapore Portfolio Divestment (completed Aug 2025) and Q4 run-rate revenue is S$655m annualised, so FY27 starts from a lower base before NA non-renewals (~4.7% of NA GRI confirmed), ~S$600m swap repricing and the S$500-600m NA divestment programme. No FY26/27 Q1 business update is in the extracted set; the next anchor refresh should use 1H FY26/27 (due late Oct 2026). NAV/unit S$1.63 at 31 Mar 2026 (price/NAV 1.10x) is a cross-check, not the valuation basis.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: dpu_5yr_cagr (per-unit distributable flow; equity/book CAGR is driven by IAS 40 revaluations and FX and by equity issuance for the FY22 MRDCT acquisition, so it is not a per-unit growth signal)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5y CAGR 3.6% and revenue 5y CAGR 8.5% versus DPU 5y CAGR 0.25%: aggregate growth since FY21 was bought with new units (US data-centre JV buy-in FY22), so per-unit growth is far below aggregate. EPS is fair-value noise and is not used.
historical_growth.notes: 'fcf' CAGRs are DPU (the owner flow per unit). DPU 13.57c (FY23) -> 12.71c (FY26); NAV/unit 1.85 -> 1.63.

base.narrative: FY27 revenue ~S$640m: Q4 FY26 run-rate (S$655m) less confirmed NA enterprise non-renewals, partly offset by ~7% Singapore reversions. DI margin slips ~1pp as S$600m of swaps reprice and leverage rises to ~37.5% post perp redemption; FY28 flat as the S$500-600m NA divestment programme is recycled at a dilutive spread before APAC/Europe redeployment. Then 1.5-2% organic growth (Singapore reversions, Japan DCs, NA re-leasing to cloud/colo).

bull.narrative: NA vacancies re-let to hyperscale/colo tenants quickly given record-low primary-market vacancy; divestment proceeds recycled accretively into Japan/APAC DCs via the sponsor pipeline; rates ease so swap resets cost less than feared. DPU troughs in FY27 and grows ~3% thereafter.

bear.narrative: Further NA enterprise non-renewals in secondary markets (San Diego the largest), slow re-letting with heavy fit-out capex, USD/JPY weakness, and divestments at cap rates well above the cost of debt. DPU falls ~4%/yr for two years (JPMorgan view) and then grows only ~1%.

scenario_narratives.base: DPU steps down again in FY27 (to ~11.9c declared, ~11.1c owner flow after unit-paid fees and maintenance capex) on NA non-renewals and swap repricing, troughs in FY28 through the divestment programme, then grows 1.5-2% a year. Capitalised at a 7.5% SGD cost of equity.
scenario_narratives.bull: FY27 is the trough: NA space re-lets to cloud/colo, recycling into Japan/APAC DCs is accretive, and DPU compounds ~3% from FY28. 7.0% cost of equity.
scenario_narratives.bear: North American enterprise data centres keep emptying, re-letting needs capex, FX and divestment dilution compound: DPU falls ~4% a year for two years and then grows ~1%. 8.0% cost of equity.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25 rather than the bull-tilted house default: DPU has fallen three years running, ~4.7% of NA GRI is already confirmed to leave in FY27 and S$600m of swaps reprice higher, so the downside is as live as the upside. The balance sheet (34.0% leverage, AA- JCR/R&I, BBB+ Fitch) rules out a solvency-type bear, which is why bear is not weighted above 25%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the per-unit distributable flow an owner actually receives, net of the management fees settled in new units and of the maintenance capex distributable income ignores, capitalised at the SGD cost of equity with no debt deduction (the flow is post-interest and post-perpetuals). NAV is a cross-check only: IAS 40 values are appraiser cap rates, and the stock trades at ~1.10x NAV.
key_risks_to_valuation: North American data centres (46.5% of AUM) carry enterprise-tenant non-renewal risk outside primary markets; re-letting speed and fit-out capex drive the bear/base gap
~S$600m of interest-rate hedges reprice in FY26/27 and leverage rises to ~37.5%; every 100bp on unhedged debt is ~S$3-7m of DI
USD and JPY translation: ~92.5% of distributable income is SGD-hedged near term, but not structurally
Capital recycling: S$500-600m of NA divestments must be redeployed at a positive spread or DPU steps down further
Cost of equity: a 50bp move in the SGD rate moves the base value by roughly 8-10%
